St. Nikodemos the Hagiorite

Saints

Saint Nikodemos the Hagiorite

St. Nicodemus the Hagiorite · St. Nicodemus of the Holy Mountain · St. Nikodemos of the Holy Mountain · St. Nikodemos the Athonite · St. Nicodemos the Hagiorite

Period
1748–1809 (OCA chronology)
Region
Naxos; Mount Athos, Greece
Titles / vocation
Monastic · Teacher
Commemoration
July 14

Introduction

Saint Nikodemos was an Athonite monk and editor whose work transmitted patristic, liturgical, and canonical texts, including the Philokalia and the Rudder.

Death / martyrdom

Peaceful repose on Mount Athos in 1809

Read circumstances and sources

Background

The OCA dates his birth on Naxos to 1748 and gives Nicholas as his baptismal name. He studied there, entered Dionysiou Monastery on Mount Athos, and received the monastic name St. Nikodemos.

[1] Published ecclesiastical biography / commemoration · Opening paragraphs: Naxos, education and Dionysiou

Life and notable events

He first worked as the monastery’s secretary. Saint Makarios of Corinth entrusted him with editing the Philokalia manuscript. Later he combined further monastic formation with extensive editorial work, including preparing writings by earlier Orthodox teachers.

[1] Published ecclesiastical biography / commemoration · Paragraphs on monastic obedience, the Philokalia and Great Schema

Death and martyrdom

In declining health he stayed with two brother iconographers, who helped him. He received the Church’s sacraments before his peaceful death on July 14, 1809. Constantinople formally glorified him in 1955; he was not a martyr.

[1] Published ecclesiastical biography / commemoration · Final paragraphs on illness and repose

Writings and legacy

His publications include a confession manual, liturgical canons, Saints’ lives, and the Rudder, a collection of Church canons prepared with a collaborator. These are different genres: pastoral counsel, hymnography, hagiography, and canon law.

[1] Published ecclesiastical biography / commemoration · Paragraphs on Exomologitarion, Theotokarion, New Martyrologion and Pedalion
